ideas.title: Say why a worker failed, stop the whole Claude Code process on a timeout, and don't pay the API to start from zero after running out of turns
ideas.problem: In workers.py run(), every failure becomes the same `Unavailable`: a timeout (`raise Unavailable("Claude Code took too long.")`), a result that is not `subtype == "success"` (this includes error_max_turns and error_max_budget_usd), no structured answer, and sign-in or plan-limit errors. The callers then log `fallback_api` and rerun the whole job on the paid API (agents.py: Sage ~line 130, Serge ~line 430). Sage is allowed max_turns=30 and Serge 15, so a slow research day can end as: 30 turns of subscription work thrown away, then a second full run on the API. Also, subprocess.run(timeout=...) only kills the process it started; on Windows Claude Code's own children (Bash tool, node, MCP) are not cleaned up, per user bug reports.
ideas.proposal: Three small changes in workers.py, nothing else. (1) Replace subprocess.run with Popen + communicate(timeout); on TimeoutExpired run `taskkill /T /F /PID <pid>` with its own 15 s timeout (Windows only), then proc.kill() and communicate() to drain. (2) After the JSON is parsed, read out['subtype']; raise `OutOfTurns(Unavailable)` for 'error_max_turns' (and keep Unavailable for others), and put the kind (timeout | out_of_turns | no_structured_answer | limit | other) in the `fallback_api` event and in the Unavailable text the office shows. (3) In sage_research and serge: on OutOfTurns, retry ONCE on the subscription with max_turns raised by 50% and the extra line 'You are short on turns: stop searching and write the brief now from what you have.' Only if that also fails, fall back to the API as today. Leave the daily allowance check and caps as they are.
ideas.gain: Fewer wasted paid API reruns and no leftover claude.exe/node.exe processes after a timeout. Measure: count `fallback_api` events by kind over two weeks (today they carry only free text); target is zero API reruns caused by out_of_turns, and no claude.exe left in Task Manager after a forced 900 s timeout.
ideas.test: (a) Normal: HQ_SIMULATE with a fake claude that returns subtype success -> no change, no fallback. (b) Edge: fake claude printing {subtype:'error_max_turns'} -> OutOfTurns raised, one subscription retry with the extra line, fallback_api kind=out_of_turns only if the retry also fails. (c) Failure: fake claude that sleeps past a short timeout after starting a child process -> on Windows both processes are gone afterwards and Unavailable says 'timeout'. Pass = all three behave as written and existing tests still pass.
ideas.confidence_why: Retry/timeouts/budget behaviour is from Anthropic's own docs (A); the Windows orphan behaviour and error_max_turns result shape rest on user bug reports (B/C), and I could not see how often it happens in our logs.
ideas.risks: workers.py is a file Ghassan must not edit, so this is a Builder-chat job. taskkill can itself hang (issue 67888), hence its own timeout. A second subscription run uses more of the daily allowance. Does not overlap idea 2026-10-07-2 (dollar cap per run): that one stops cost, this one changes what happens after a stop. If the owner says yes to both, apply them together in the same function.
